## Purpose and configuration

This notebook simulates symmetric networks and evaluates Theorem 1 at one
selected node and Theorem 2 for the global symmetric parameter $\Lambda$.
It supports Gaussian, Poisson, Bernoulli-logit, and Bernoulli-probit observations.
The YAML parameters above control the experiment; non-`null` entries override
the model defaults in `default_model_configs()`.

- `n_sim` is the number of simulated networks. `max_iter` limits optimizer
  updates within a single network fit.
- `target_node` selects the node for Theorem 1. Theorem 2 concerns the global
  parameter and does not depend on this node selection.
- `k` is the latent dimension $K$. If it is `null`, the code infers $K$ from
  `lambda_values`; otherwise the two dimensions must agree. The true matrix is
  $\Lambda^\star=\operatorname{diag}(\texttt{lambda\_values})$.
- `design_seed` determines the latent design. Network replication $r$ uses
  `replication_seed_base + r`. Changing the latter leaves the latent truth fixed.
- `run_simulation: false` constructs and checks the truth without running
  Monte Carlo replications or saving their outputs. It does not reload CSVs.

Use the YAML header as the record of the selected experiment, and update
`output_dir` when changing its settings. When knitted in RStudio, relative
paths start from this notebook's `simulations/` directory. For `model: "all"`,
give a common output directory; the code adds one subdirectory per model.
The models run sequentially, with at most seven workers within each model.

## Fixed latent design and network generation

The rejection sampler is adapted from
[DLSM/simulation.R](https://github.com/yatian20/DLSM/blob/main/simulation.R).
It draws independent candidate coordinates uniformly on $[-1,1]^K$ and retains
rows satisfying $\lVert z_i\rVert<1$. Repeated batches provide exactly $n$
retained rows, each uniformly distributed in the unit ball. The default batch
size is $\min(50000,n2^K)$; acceptance becomes less efficient as $K$ increases.

This notebook then constructs its required latent matrix by **uncentered
second-moment whitening**:
\[
  U^\star=Z\left(\frac{Z^\top Z}{n}\right)^{-1/2},
  \qquad (U^\star)^\top U^\star=nI_K.
\]
No sample mean is subtracted. The shared whitening transform makes the rows of
$U^\star$ dependent, and their norms need not remain below one. At fixed $n$
and $K$, the same design seed reproduces the same latent matrix. Using the same
seed at different sample sizes does not guarantee nested latent designs.

Within a setting, $U^\star$ and $\Lambda^\star$ stay fixed across replications.
Each replication generates independent upper-triangle observations conditional
on $\theta_{ij}^\star=(u_i^\star)^\top\Lambda^\star u_j^\star$, mirrors them to
the lower triangle, and sets the diagonal to zero. There is no separate
intercept or node-effect term. When all four models are requested, the code
checks that they use the same $U^\star$.

## Statistics and saved results

Estimates are aligned to the known truth before evaluating the simulation
errors. This alignment uses information available in simulations. The practical
interface for an observed dataset is provided separately in `gfm_estimation.R`.

Each results CSV has one row per attempted network replication:

| Columns | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `stat_U_1`, ..., `stat_U_K` | Theorem 1 standardized error components for `target_node`. |
| `raw_lambda_j`, `debiased_lambda_j` | Standardized errors before and after the Lambda correction. |
| `lambda_raw_error_j`, `lambda_debiased_error_j` | Errors in the unstandardized `lambda_v` coordinates. |
| `chi_sq_U`, `chi_sq_debiased_lambda` | Squared norms of the corresponding standardized vectors. |
| `convergence_code`, `n_iter` | Replication status and number of optimizer updates. |

Status codes are 0 (success), 1 (iteration limit), 2 (non-finite optimizer result),
and 3 (a caught error during fitting or inference).

Here $d=K(K+1)/2$ Lambda components are stored using the coordinate convention
documented in `get_lambda_v()`. The joint reference laws are $\chi^2_K$ for
Theorem 1 and $\chi^2_d$ for the bias-corrected Theorem 2 statistic. Components
are summarized separately. QQ titles and console summaries report sample
**standard deviations** (`sd`), not variances or Monte Carlo standard errors.

Failed or nonconverged replications remain in the CSV with status codes and
missing inference statistics; the default summaries and QQ plots use successful
replications. The output also includes the complete R object, truth,
configuration, execution settings, and a QQ-plot PDF when plotting is possible.
Retain the configuration alongside a CSV when sharing or replotting results.

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Symmetric latent-factor network simulation with configurable dimension k.
# Raw rows z_i are iid uniform in the unit k-ball. Uncentered whitening gives
# U_star^T U_star = n I_k, couples the rows, and does not impose zero means.
# Hold U_star and Lambda_star fixed; redraw the edge observations for each fit.

library(doParallel)
library(foreach)

# Supply fallback runtime parameters when extracted R code is sourced.
# Existing params entries take precedence, including explicit NULL values.
# Supply a valid n/target_node combination; the bare fallbacks are not
# a complete runnable experiment. The YAML above supplies these overrides.
default_runtime_params <- list(
  model = "all",
  run_simulation = FALSE,
  n = NULL,
  n_sim = NULL,
  k = NULL,
  lambda_values = "0.40, 0.35",
  design_seed = NULL,
  replication_seed_base = NULL,
  target_node = NULL,
  sigma = NULL,
  learning_rate = NULL,
  max_iter = NULL,
  tolerance = NULL,
  M_bound_U = NULL,
  M_bound_Lambda = NULL,
  probability_eps = NULL,
  probability_floor = NULL,
  curvature_floor = NULL,
  node_information_floor = NULL,
  whitening_eigen_floor = NULL,
  truth_check_action = "error",
  n_cores = NULL,
  output_dir = NULL
)
runtime_params <- default_runtime_params
if (exists("params", inherits = FALSE)) {
  supplied_param_names <- intersect(names(default_runtime_params), names(params))
  runtime_params[supplied_param_names] <- params[supplied_param_names]
}

# Pin the RNG algorithms for reproducible random draws.
# design_seed fixes the latent design; replication r uses
# replication_seed_base + r, independently of worker scheduling.
set_reproducible_seed <- function(seed) {
  RNGkind(
    kind = "Mersenne-Twister",
    normal.kind = "Inversion",
    sample.kind = "Rejection"
  )
  set.seed(as.integer(seed))
}

RNGkind(
  kind = "Mersenne-Twister",
  normal.kind = "Inversion",
  sample.kind = "Rejection"
)

# -------------------------- Configuration ------------------------

# Resolve supported aliases to a single model name used by all routines.
normalize_model_name <- function(model) {
  key <- tolower(gsub("[- ]", "_", model))
  aliases <- c(
    logit = "bernoulli_logit",
    bernoulli_logit = "bernoulli_logit",
    probit = "bernoulli_probit",
    bernoulli_probit = "bernoulli_probit",
    gaussian = "gaussian",
    normal = "gaussian",
    poisson = "poisson"
  )
  if (!key %in% names(aliases)) {
    stop(
      "Unknown model: ", model,
      ". Choose bernoulli_logit, bernoulli_probit, gaussian, or poisson."
    )
  }
  unname(aliases[[key]])
}

# Parse the requested diagonal of Lambda_star from numeric or YAML input.
parse_lambda_values <- function(value) {
  if (is.null(value)) return(NULL)

  # Accept an R numeric vector/list, YAML [a, b, ...], or a comma-separated
  # character value supplied programmatically.
  if (is.character(value)) {
    pieces <- unlist(strsplit(
      gsub("\\[|\\]", "", paste(value, collapse = ",")),
      split = ",",
      fixed = TRUE
    ), use.names = FALSE)
    pieces <- trimws(pieces)
    pieces <- pieces[nzchar(pieces)]
    lambda_vec <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(pieces))
  } else {
    if (is.logical(value) ||
        (is.list(value) && any(vapply(value, is.null, logical(1L))))) {
      stop("lambda_values cannot contain logical or NULL entries.")
    }
    flattened <- unlist(value, recursive = TRUE, use.names = FALSE)
    if (!is.numeric(flattened) || is.logical(flattened)) {
      stop("lambda_values entries must all be numeric.")
    }
    lambda_vec <- as.numeric(flattened)
  }

  if (!length(lambda_vec) || any(!is.finite(lambda_vec))) {
    stop("lambda_values must contain at least one finite numeric value.")
  }
  unname(lambda_vec)
}

# Resolve K and the true diagonal coefficients, requiring matching lengths.
resolve_latent_parameters <- function(base_config, k_value, lambda_values) {
  lambda_vec <- parse_lambda_values(lambda_values)

  if (is.null(k_value)) {
    k <- if (is.null(lambda_vec)) base_config$k else length(lambda_vec)
  } else {
    k_numeric <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(k_value))
    if (length(k_numeric) != 1L || !is.finite(k_numeric) ||
        k_numeric < 1 || k_numeric != floor(k_numeric) ||
        k_numeric > .Machine$integer.max) {
      stop("k must be one positive integer or NULL.")
    }
    k <- as.integer(k_numeric)
  }

  if (is.null(lambda_vec)) {
    if (k != base_config$k) {
      stop(
        "When k differs from its model default, provide lambda_values ",
        "with exactly k entries."
      )
    }
    lambda_vec <- base_config$lambda_vec
  }
  if (length(lambda_vec) != k) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "k=%d but lambda_values contains %d entries.",
      k, length(lambda_vec)
    ))
  }

  list(k = as.integer(k), lambda_vec = lambda_vec)
}

# Apply named overrides, validate the configuration, and cast integer fields.
get_model_config <- function(model, overrides = list()) {
  model <- normalize_model_name(model)
  config <- default_model_configs()[[model]]
  if (length(overrides)) {
    unknown <- setdiff(names(overrides), names(config))
    if (length(unknown)) {
      stop("Unknown configuration field(s): ", paste(unknown, collapse = ", "))
    }
    config[names(overrides)] <- overrides
  }
  validate_model_config(config)
  integer_fields <- c(
    "n", "k", "n_sim", "max_iter", "target_node",
    "design_seed", "replication_seed_base"
  )
  config[integer_fields] <- lapply(config[integer_fields], as.integer)
  config
}

# Reject incompatible dimensions, seeds, bounds, and simulation controls.
validate_model_config <- function(config) {
  integer_fields <- c(
    "n", "k", "n_sim", "max_iter", "target_node",
    "design_seed", "replication_seed_base"
  )
  valid_integer_scalar <- function(x) {
    length(x) == 1L && is.finite(x) && x == floor(x) &&
      abs(x) <= .Machine$integer.max
  }
  invalid_integer_fields <- integer_fields[!vapply(
    config[integer_fields], valid_integer_scalar, logical(1L)
  )]
  if (length(invalid_integer_fields)) {
    stop(
      "These fields must be finite integer scalars: ",
      paste(invalid_integer_fields, collapse = ", ")
    )
  }
  if (config$n <= config$k || config$k < 1L) stop("Require n > k >= 1.")
  if (length(config$lambda_vec) != config$k ||
      any(!is.finite(config$lambda_vec))) {
    stop("lambda_vec must contain k finite values.")
  }
  lambda_scale <- max(abs(config$lambda_vec), 1)
  if (min(abs(config$lambda_vec)) <=
      sqrt(.Machine$double.eps) * lambda_scale) {
    stop(
      "Every lambda value must be nonzero at numerical precision so that ",
      "the k latent directions are identifiable."
    )
  }
  if (config$n_sim < 1L || config$max_iter < 1L) {
    stop("n_sim and max_iter must be positive.")
  }
  if (!is.finite(config$learning_rate) ||
      !is.finite(config$tolerance) ||
      config$learning_rate <= 0 || config$tolerance <= 0) {
    stop("learning_rate and tolerance must be positive.")
  }
  if (!is.finite(config$M_bound_U) ||
      config$M_bound_U < sqrt(config$k)) {
    stop("M_bound_U must be finite and at least sqrt(k).")
  }
  if (!is.finite(config$M_bound_Lambda) ||
      config$M_bound_Lambda < max(abs(config$lambda_vec))) {
    stop(
      "M_bound_Lambda must be finite and at least max(abs(lambda_vec))."
    )
  }
  if (!is.finite(config$probability_eps) ||
      config$probability_eps <= 0 || config$probability_eps >= 0.5) {
    stop("probability_eps must lie strictly between 0 and 0.5.")
  }
  maximum_seed <- .Machine$integer.max
  if (config$design_seed < 0 || config$design_seed > maximum_seed ||
      config$replication_seed_base < 0 ||
      config$replication_seed_base > maximum_seed - config$n_sim) {
    stop(
      "Seeds must be nonnegative integers, and replication_seed_base + ",
      "n_sim must not exceed .Machine$integer.max."
    )
  }
  if (config$target_node < 1L || config$target_node > config$n) {
    stop("target_node must lie in 1,...,n.")
  }
  if (length(config$sigma) != 1L || !is.finite(config$sigma)) {
    stop("sigma must be a finite scalar.")
  }
  if (config$model == "gaussian" && config$sigma <= 0) {
    stop("Gaussian sigma must be positive.")
  }
  if (!config$truth_check_action %in% c("warning", "error", "none")) {
    stop("truth_check_action must be warning, error, or none.")
  }
  if (!is.finite(config$whitening_eigen_floor) ||
      config$whitening_eigen_floor <= 0) {
    stop("whitening_eigen_floor must be positive.")
  }
  if (!is.na(config$probability_floor) &&
      (!is.finite(config$probability_floor) ||
       config$probability_floor <= 0 || config$probability_floor >= 0.5)) {
    stop("probability_floor must be NA or lie strictly between 0 and 0.5.")
  }
  if (!is.na(config$curvature_floor) &&
      (!is.finite(config$curvature_floor) || config$curvature_floor <= 0)) {
    stop("curvature_floor must be NA or positive.")
  }
  if (!is.na(config$node_information_floor) &&
      (!is.finite(config$node_information_floor) ||
       config$node_information_floor <= 0)) {
    stop("node_information_floor must be NA or positive.")
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# --------------------------- Utilities ---------------------------

# Remove numerical asymmetry by averaging a matrix with its transpose.
symmetrize <- function(A) (A + t(A)) / 2

# Evaluate logistic probabilities without overflowing for large |x|.
sigmoid <- function(x) {
  out <- numeric(length(x))
  positive <- x >= 0
  out[positive] <- 1 / (1 + exp(-x[positive]))
  exp_x <- exp(x[!positive])
  out[!positive] <- exp_x / (1 + exp_x)
  dim(out) <- dim(x)
  out
}

# Evaluate log(1 + exp(x)) stably for the logit likelihood.
stable_log1pexp <- function(x) {
  pmax(x, 0) + log1p(exp(-abs(x)))
}

# Form a PSD pseudoinverse after dropping n_drop eigenvalues nearest zero.
# Invert eigenvalues above the relative threshold; reject substantial
# negative eigenvalues instead of concealing indefiniteness.
safe_pinv_psd <- function(
  A, n_drop = 0L, rel_tol = 1e-10, negative_tol = 1e-7
) {
  A <- symmetrize(A)
  eg <- eigen(A, symmetric = TRUE)
  vals <- eg$values
  p <- length(vals)
  if (any(!is.finite(vals))) stop("Non-finite information eigenvalue.")
  if (n_drop < 0L || n_drop > p) stop("Invalid n_drop.")
  if (p == 0L || n_drop == p) return(matrix(0, p, p))

  scale <- max(abs(vals))
  if (scale == 0) return(matrix(0, p, p))
  if (min(vals) < -negative_tol * scale) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "Matrix expected to be PSD has min eigenvalue %.4e (scale %.4e).",
      min(vals), scale
    ))
  }

  keep <- rep(TRUE, p)
  if (n_drop > 0L) {
    keep[order(abs(vals))[seq_len(n_drop)]] <- FALSE
  }
  keep <- keep & vals > rel_tol * scale
  vals_inv <- numeric(p)
  vals_inv[keep] <- 1 / vals[keep]
  symmetrize(eg$vectors %*% diag(vals_inv, p) %*% t(eg$vectors))
}

# Compute the symmetric PSD square root used to standardize estimation errors.
safe_sqrt_psd <- function(A, rel_tol = 1e-10, negative_tol = 1e-7) {
  A <- symmetrize(A)
  eg <- eigen(A, symmetric = TRUE)
  vals <- eg$values
  if (any(!is.finite(vals))) stop("Non-finite covariance eigenvalue.")
  scale <- max(abs(vals))
  if (scale == 0) return(matrix(0, nrow(A), ncol(A)))
  if (min(vals) < -negative_tol * scale) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "Matrix expected to be PSD has min eigenvalue %.4e (scale %.4e).",
      min(vals), scale
    ))
  }
  vals[vals < rel_tol * scale] <- 0
  symmetrize(eg$vectors %*% diag(sqrt(vals), length(vals)) %*% t(eg$vectors))
}

# Require numerical positive definiteness and return the checked eigenvalues.
assert_positive_definite <- function(
  A, label = "Information matrix", rel_tol = 1e-10
) {
  values <- eigen(
    symmetrize(A), symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE
  )$values
  if (!length(values) || any(!is.finite(values))) {
    stop(label, " has non-finite or missing eigenvalues.")
  }
  scale <- max(abs(values))
  if (scale == 0 || min(values) <= rel_tol * scale) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "%s is not numerically positive definite: min %.4e, max scale %.4e.",
      label, min(values), scale
    ))
  }
  invisible(values)
}

# Invert a positive-definite matrix by Cholesky and report conditioning checks.
ordinary_inverse_pd <- function(
  A, label = "Information matrix", rel_tol = 1e-10
) {
  A <- symmetrize(A)
  values <- assert_positive_definite(A, label, rel_tol)
  inverse <- symmetrize(chol2inv(chol(A)))
  inverse_residual <- max(abs(A %*% inverse - diag(nrow(A))))
  list(
    inverse = inverse,
    eigenvalues = values,
    min_eigenvalue = min(values),
    max_eigenvalue = max(values),
    condition_number = max(values) / min(values),
    inverse_residual = inverse_residual
  )
}

# Compute a symmetric inverse square root without eigenvalue clipping.
# Require min(eigenvalue) > eigen_floor * max(eigenvalue).
symmetric_inverse_sqrt <- function(A, eigen_floor = 1e-10) {
  A <- symmetrize(A)
  eg <- eigen(A, symmetric = TRUE)
  vals <- eg$values
  if (any(!is.finite(vals)) || max(vals) <= 0) {
    stop("The uncentered sample second-moment matrix is not positive definite.")
  }
  threshold <- eigen_floor * max(vals)
  if (min(vals) <= threshold) {
    stop(sprintf(
      paste0(
        "The uncentered sample second-moment matrix is too ill-conditioned: ",
        "min eigenvalue %.4e, threshold %.4e."
      ),
      min(vals), threshold
    ))
  }
  symmetrize(
    eg$vectors %*% diag(1 / sqrt(vals), length(vals)) %*% t(eg$vectors)
  )
}

# Vectorize symmetric Lambda: diagonal / sqrt(2), then upper entries by row.
# For K=3 the entry order is 11, 22, 33, 12, 13, 23; d=K*(K+1)/2.
get_lambda_v <- function(Lambda) {
  k <- nrow(Lambda)
  out <- diag(Lambda) / sqrt(2)
  if (k >= 2L) {
    for (a in seq_len(k - 1L)) {
      for (b in seq.int(a + 1L, k)) out <- c(out, Lambda[a, b])
    }
  }
  as.vector(out)
}

# Differentiate u_i^T Lambda u_j in the get_lambda_v() coordinate order.
lambda_direction_derivative <- function(ui, uj) {
  k <- length(ui)
  out <- sqrt(2) * ui * uj
  if (k >= 2L) {
    for (a in seq_len(k - 1L)) {
      for (b in seq.int(a + 1L, k)) {
        out <- c(out, ui[a] * uj[b] + ui[b] * uj[a])
      }
    }
  }
  as.vector(out)
}

# Return a certified joint projection when the scaled polar factor is feasible;
# stop if its row norms violate the bound, since row clipping is not equivalent.
project_C_U_certified <- function(
  Z, bound, row_tolerance = 1e-10, gram_tolerance = 1e-10,
  objective_tolerance = 1e-10, context = ""
) {
  if (!is.matrix(Z) || !is.numeric(Z) || any(!is.finite(Z))) {
    stop("Z must be a finite numeric matrix in the C_U projection.")
  }
  n <- nrow(Z)
  k <- ncol(Z)
  if (k < 1L || n < k || length(bound) != 1L ||
      !is.finite(bound) || bound < sqrt(k)) {
    stop("C_U is infeasible: require n >= k and M_bound_U >= sqrt(k).")
  }

  # The scaled polar factor is a global Euclidean projection onto
  # {U: U^T U = n I_k}. If it also satisfies the row-norm bound, it is
  # therefore a global projection onto the intersection C_U. When the row
  # bound is active, clipping would destroy U^T U = n I_k; fail explicitly
  # instead of silently replacing the theoretical joint projection.
  decomposition <- svd(Z, nu = k, nv = k)
  U <- sqrt(n) * decomposition$u[, seq_len(k), drop = FALSE] %*%
    t(decomposition$v[, seq_len(k), drop = FALSE])
  gram_error <- max(abs(crossprod(U) / n - diag(k)))
  max_row_norm <- max(sqrt(rowSums(U^2)))
  row_violation <- max(0, max_row_norm - bound)
  objective <- 0.5 * sum((U - Z)^2)
  stiefel_lower_bound <- 0.5 * (
    sum(Z^2) + n * k - 2 * sqrt(n) * sum(decomposition$d)
  )
  objective_gap <- abs(objective - stiefel_lower_bound)
  objective_scale <- max(1, abs(objective), abs(stiefel_lower_bound))
  if (gram_error > gram_tolerance) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "The scaled-polar projection failed its Gram check: %.4e > %.4e.",
      gram_error, gram_tolerance
    ))
  }
  if (objective_gap > objective_tolerance * objective_scale) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "The scaled-polar objective certificate failed: gap %.4e.",
      objective_gap
    ))
  }
  if (row_violation > row_tolerance * max(1, bound)) {
    message_text <- sprintf(
      paste0(
        "Certified joint C_U projection unavailable%s: scaled-polar row ",
        "norm %.16g exceeds M_bound_U %.16g by %.4e. The run must stop; ",
        "row clipping is not a joint Euclidean projection."
      ),
      if (nzchar(context)) paste0(" [", context, "]") else "",
      max_row_norm, bound, row_violation
    )
    condition <- structure(
      list(
        message = message_text, call = NULL, context = context,
        row_max = max_row_norm, bound = bound,
        row_violation = row_violation, gram_error = gram_error,
        objective_gap = objective_gap
      ),
      class = c("active_U_row_bound", "error", "condition")
    )
    stop(condition)
  }

  list(
    U = U,
    method = "polar_exact",
    max_row_norm = max_row_norm,
    max_row_ratio = max_row_norm / bound,
    row_violation = row_violation,
    row_margin = bound - max_row_norm,
    gram_error = gram_error,
    objective_gap = objective_gap
  )
}

# Project symmetric Lambda onto the operator-norm ball by clipping eigenvalues.
proximal_projection_Lambda <- function(Lambda, bound) {
  eg <- eigen(symmetrize(Lambda), symmetric = TRUE)
  vals <- pmax(pmin(eg$values, bound), -bound)
  symmetrize(eg$vectors %*% diag(vals, length(vals)) %*% t(eg$vectors))
}

# Measure the U and lambda_v projected updates relative to their actual steps.
projected_gradient_mapping_components <- function(
  U, U_next, Lambda, Lambda_next, learning_rate, n
) {
  if (!is.finite(learning_rate) || learning_rate <= 0 ||
      !is.finite(n) || n <= 0) {
    stop("learning_rate and n must be positive in the residual calculation.")
  }
  eta_U <- learning_rate / n
  eta_Lambda_v <- learning_rate / (2 * n^2)
  c(
    U = max(abs(U_next - U)) / eta_U,
    Lambda_v = max(abs(
      get_lambda_v(Lambda_next) - get_lambda_v(Lambda)
    )) / eta_Lambda_v
  )
}

# --------------------- Distribution quantities ------------------

# Compute probit probabilities and stable density-to-tail ratios:
# a = phi(theta)/Phi(theta), b = phi(theta)/(1 - Phi(theta)).
probit_ratios <- function(theta) {
  log_phi <- dnorm(theta, log = TRUE)
  log_p1 <- pnorm(theta, log.p = TRUE)
  log_p0 <- pnorm(theta, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
  list(
    p1 = pnorm(theta),
    p0 = pnorm(theta, lower.tail = FALSE),
    a = exp(log_phi - log_p1),
    b = exp(log_phi - log_p0),
    log_phi = log_phi,
    log_p1 = log_p1,
    log_p0 = log_p0
  )
}

# Map predictors to edge means (probabilities only for the Bernoulli models).
link_probability <- function(theta, config) {
  switch(
    config$model,
    bernoulli_logit = sigmoid(theta),
    bernoulli_probit = pnorm(theta),
    poisson = exp(theta),
    gaussian = theta
  )
}

# Transform initial edge-mean estimates to predictors, with model-specific clips.
link_inverse <- function(value, config, eps = config$probability_eps) {
  switch(
    config$model,
    bernoulli_logit = {
      p <- pmax(pmin(value, 1 - eps), eps)
      log(p / (1 - p))
    },
    bernoulli_probit = qnorm(pmax(pmin(value, 1 - eps), eps)),
    poisson = log(pmax(value, 0.1)),
    gaussian = value
  )
}

# Sum negative edge log-likelihoods, omitting terms constant in the parameters.
negative_loglikelihood_edges <- function(theta, y, config) {
  switch(
    config$model,
    bernoulli_logit = sum(stable_log1pexp(theta) - y * theta),
    bernoulli_probit = {
      log_p1 <- pnorm(theta, log.p = TRUE)
      log_p0 <- pnorm(theta, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
      -sum(ifelse(y > 0.5, log_p1, log_p0))
    },
    gaussian = sum((theta - y)^2) / (2 * config$sigma^2),
    poisson = sum(exp(theta) - y * theta)
  )
}

# Compute elementwise derivatives of the negative log-likelihood in theta.
negative_score_matrix <- function(theta, A, config) {
  switch(
    config$model,
    bernoulli_logit = sigmoid(theta) - A,
    bernoulli_probit = {
      r <- probit_ratios(theta)
      out <- ifelse(A > 0.5, -r$a, r$b)
      dim(out) <- dim(theta)
      out
    },
    gaussian = (theta - A) / config$sigma^2,
    poisson = exp(theta) - A
  )
}

# For the edge log-likelihood ell(theta; y), return information = -E[ell''],
# E[ell'''], and E[ell' * ell'']; outcome-specific information is -ell''.
# These use log-likelihood signs, whereas negative_score_matrix()
# differentiates the negative log-likelihood used by the optimizer.
expected_derivative_terms <- function(theta, config) {
  zero <- 0 * theta

  if (config$model == "bernoulli_logit") {
    p <- sigmoid(theta)
    information <- p * (1 - p)
    expected_ell3 <- -information * (1 - 2 * p)
    return(list(
      mean_parameter = p,
      information = information,
      expected_ell3 = expected_ell3,
      expected_score_ell2 = zero,
      observed_information_y1 = information,
      observed_information_y0 = information
    ))
  }

  if (config$model == "bernoulli_probit") {
    r <- probit_ratios(theta)
    a <- r$a
    b <- r$b
    ell2_1 <- -theta * a - a^2
    ell3_1 <- a * (theta^2 - 1) + 3 * theta * a^2 + 2 * a^3
    ell2_0 <- theta * b - b^2
    ell3_0 <- b * (1 - theta^2) + 3 * theta * b^2 - 2 * b^3
    information <- exp(2 * r$log_phi - r$log_p1 - r$log_p0)
    return(list(
      mean_parameter = r$p1,
      information = information,
      expected_ell3 = information * (3 * theta + 2 * a - 2 * b),
      expected_score_ell2 = information * (b - a - theta),
      observed_information_y1 = -ell2_1,
      observed_information_y0 = -ell2_0,
      ell3_y1 = ell3_1,
      ell3_y0 = ell3_0
    ))
  }

  if (config$model == "gaussian") {
    return(list(
      mean_parameter = theta,
      information = zero + 1 / config$sigma^2,
      expected_ell3 = zero,
      expected_score_ell2 = zero,
      observed_information_y1 = zero + 1 / config$sigma^2,
      observed_information_y0 = zero + 1 / config$sigma^2
    ))
  }

  intensity <- exp(theta)
  list(
    mean_parameter = intensity,
    information = intensity,
    expected_ell3 = -intensity,
    expected_score_ell2 = zero,
    observed_information_y1 = intensity,
    observed_information_y0 = intensity
  )
}

# These deterministic identities protect the probit branch from silently
# reverting to the Bernoulli variance p(1-p), which is not the probit Fisher
# weight. This check is fast and runs once when the Rmd is sourced or knitted.
validate_probit_derivatives <- function(tolerance = 5e-7) {
  theta <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 121L)
  config <- default_model_configs()$bernoulli_probit
  r <- probit_ratios(theta)
  terms <- expected_derivative_terms(theta, config)
  expected_observed <- r$p1 * terms$observed_information_y1 +
    r$p0 * terms$observed_information_y0
  score_mean <- r$p1 * r$a + r$p0 * (-r$b)
  expected_ell3_outcome <- r$p1 * terms$ell3_y1 + r$p0 * terms$ell3_y0
  ell2_y1 <- -terms$observed_information_y1
  ell2_y0 <- -terms$observed_information_y0
  expected_score_ell2_outcome <-
    r$p1 * r$a * ell2_y1 + r$p0 * (-r$b) * ell2_y0

  h <- 1e-5
  numerical_negative_score_y1 <- (
    -pnorm(theta + h, log.p = TRUE) + pnorm(theta - h, log.p = TRUE)
  ) / (2 * h)
  numerical_negative_score_y0 <- (
    -pnorm(theta + h, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE) +
      pnorm(theta - h, lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
  ) / (2 * h)

  errors <- c(
    fisher = max(abs(expected_observed - terms$information)),
    mean_score = max(abs(score_mean)),
    higher_moment = max(
      abs(expected_ell3_outcome - terms$expected_ell3),
      abs(expected_score_ell2_outcome - terms$expected_score_ell2)
    ),
    symmetry = max(
      abs(terms$information - rev(terms$information)),
      abs(terms$expected_ell3 + rev(terms$expected_ell3)),
      abs(terms$expected_score_ell2 + rev(terms$expected_score_ell2))
    ),
    numerical_gradient = max(
      abs(numerical_negative_score_y1 + r$a),
      abs(numerical_negative_score_y0 - r$b)
    )
  )
  if (any(!is.finite(errors)) || max(errors) > tolerance) {
    stop(
      "Probit derivative self-check failed: ",
      paste(sprintf("%s=%.3e", names(errors), errors), collapse = ", ")
    )
  }
  invisible(errors)
}

validate_probit_derivatives()

# Evaluate the realized negative second derivative for each observed edge.
observed_information_matrix <- function(theta, config, A = NULL) {
  # For Gaussian, logit, and Poisson, the observed negative Hessian is
  # identical to the expected Fisher information.  Probit is different:
  # its observed curvature depends on the realized binary outcome.
  if (config$model != "bernoulli_probit") {
    return(expected_derivative_terms(theta, config)$information)
  }

  if (is.null(A)) {
    stop("A is required for the observed probit information matrix.")
  }
  if (!identical(dim(A), dim(theta))) {
    stop("A and theta must have the same dimensions.")
  }

  r <- probit_ratios(theta)
  information_y1 <- r$a * (theta + r$a)
  information_y0 <- r$b * (r$b - theta)
  information <- ifelse(A > 0.5, information_y1, information_y0)
  dim(information) <- dim(theta)

  # Both expressions are nonnegative analytically.  Remove only negative
  # roundoff caused by tail-ratio cancellation.
  pmax(information, 0)
}

# -------------------- Truth and data generation -----------------

# Rejection sampling adapted from:
# https://github.com/yatian20/DLSM/blob/main/simulation.R
# Accepted rows are iid uniform in the UNIT K-ball:
# E(z_i)=0, E(z_i z_i^T)=I_k/(k+2), and ||z_i||<1.
# Use repeated bounded batches so a short batch never creates missing rows.
# The default batch size is min(50000, n*2^k); batch_size can be supplied
# for diagnostic runs. Acceptance counts include unused accepted rows
# in the final batch, while the returned Z always contains exactly n rows.
sample_unit_ball_rejection <- function(n, k, batch_size = NULL) {
  positive_integer <- function(x) {
    is.numeric(x) && length(x) == 1L && is.finite(x) &&
      x >= 1 && x == floor(x) && x <= .Machine$integer.max
  }
  if (!positive_integer(n) || !positive_integer(k) || n <= k) {
    stop("Ball-rejection design requires integer n > k >= 1.")
  }
  if (is.null(batch_size)) batch_size <- min(50000, n * 2^k)
  if (!positive_integer(batch_size) || batch_size > 50000) {
    stop("batch_size must be an integer between 1 and 50000.")
  }
  n <- as.integer(n)
  k <- as.integer(k)
  batch_size <- as.integer(batch_size)
  Z <- matrix(0, nrow = n, ncol = k)
  filled <- 0L
  candidate_count <- accepted_count <- batch_count <- 0
  while (filled < n) {
    candidates <- matrix(
      runif(as.double(batch_size) * k, -1, 1),
      nrow = batch_size, ncol = k
    )
    accepted <- candidates[rowSums(candidates^2) < 1, , drop = FALSE]
    candidate_count <- candidate_count + batch_size
    accepted_count <- accepted_count + nrow(accepted)
    batch_count <- batch_count + 1
    take <- min(n - filled, nrow(accepted))
    if (take > 0L) {
      Z[filled + seq_len(take), ] <- accepted[seq_len(take), , drop = FALSE]
      filled <- filled + take
    }
  }
  list(
    Z = Z,
    candidate_count = candidate_count,
    accepted_count = accepted_count,
    batch_count = batch_count,
    acceptance_rate = accepted_count / candidate_count
  )
}

# Whiten the uncentered empirical second moment: U = Z (Z^T Z/n)^(-1/2).
# This enforces U^T U = n I_k without centering or additional scaling.
# The shared empirical transform makes the rows dependent; their norms
# need not remain below one. Return U_star and construction diagnostics.
generate_uniform_ball_rejection_whitened_no_centering_U <- function(
  n, k, design_seed, eigen_floor = 1e-10
) {
  set_reproducible_seed(design_seed)
  sampled <- sample_unit_ball_rejection(n, k)
  Z <- sampled$Z
  raw_radius_bound <- 1
  raw_row_norms <- sqrt(rowSums(Z^2))

  sample_second_moment <- crossprod(Z) / n
  inverse_sqrt <- symmetric_inverse_sqrt(
    sample_second_moment, eigen_floor
  )
  U <- Z %*% inverse_sqrt

  second_moment_eigenvalues <- sort(
    eigen(
      sample_second_moment, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE
    )$values
  )
  list(
    U_star = U,
    diagnostics = list(
      truth_design = "uniform_ball_rejection_whitened_no_centering",
      sampling_method = "cube_rejection_unit_ball",
      rejection_candidate_count = sampled$candidate_count,
      rejection_accepted_count = sampled$accepted_count,
      rejection_batch_count = sampled$batch_count,
      rejection_acceptance_rate = sampled$acceptance_rate,
      design_seed = as.integer(design_seed),
      raw_ball_radius_bound = raw_radius_bound,
      raw_max_abs_entry = max(abs(Z)),
      raw_max_row_norm = max(raw_row_norms),
      raw_row_norm_quantiles = unname(quantile(
        raw_row_norms, probs = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)
      )),
      raw_max_abs_column_mean = max(abs(colMeans(Z))),
      sample_second_moment_eigenvalues = second_moment_eigenvalues,
      sample_second_moment_condition_number =
        max(second_moment_eigenvalues) / min(second_moment_eigenvalues),
      whitened_max_abs_column_mean = max(abs(colMeans(U))),
      whitened_gram_max_abs_error =
        max(abs(crossprod(U) - n * diag(k))),
      whitened_max_row_norm = max(sqrt(rowSums(U^2)))
    )
  )
}

# Summarize the realized latent design, edge ranges, and oracle node information.
calculate_truth_diagnostics <- function(
  U_star, Lambda_star, Theta_star, config, design_diagnostics
) {
  n <- nrow(U_star)
  k <- ncol(U_star)
  upper <- upper.tri(Theta_star, diag = FALSE)
  target_other <- setdiff(seq_len(n), config$target_node)
  terms <- expected_derivative_terms(Theta_star, config)
  mean_parameter <- terms$mean_parameter
  expected_information <- terms$information
  worst_outcome_observed_curvature <- pmin(
    terms$observed_information_y1,
    terms$observed_information_y0
  )

  if (any(!is.finite(c(
    Theta_star[upper], mean_parameter[upper],
    expected_information[upper],
    worst_outcome_observed_curvature[upper]
  )))) {
    stop("The generated truth contains a non-finite model quantity.")
  }

  W <- U_star %*% Lambda_star
  target_W <- W[target_other, , drop = FALSE]
  target_information <- expected_information[
    config$target_node, target_other
  ]
  oracle_node_information <- symmetrize(
    crossprod(target_W, target_information * target_W)
  )
  lambda_operator_norm <- max(abs(
    eigen(Lambda_star, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
  ))
  maximum_row_norm <- max(sqrt(rowSums(U_star^2)))
  is_bernoulli <- config$model %in%
    c("bernoulli_logit", "bernoulli_probit")

  c(
    design_diagnostics,
    list(
      n = n,
      k = k,
      model = config$model,
      target_node = config$target_node,
      target_position = as.numeric(U_star[config$target_node, ]),
      lambda_values = diag(Lambda_star),
      maximum_row_norm = maximum_row_norm,
      gram_max_abs_error = max(abs(crossprod(U_star) - n * diag(k))),
      lambda_operator_norm = lambda_operator_norm,
      global_theta_range = range(Theta_star[upper]),
      target_theta_range = range(
        Theta_star[config$target_node, target_other]
      ),
      global_mean_parameter_range = range(mean_parameter[upper]),
      target_mean_parameter_range = range(
        mean_parameter[config$target_node, target_other]
      ),
      global_probability_range = if (is_bernoulli) {
        range(mean_parameter[upper])
      } else c(NA_real_, NA_real_),
      target_probability_range = if (is_bernoulli) {
        range(mean_parameter[config$target_node, target_other])
      } else c(NA_real_, NA_real_),
      global_min_bernoulli_variance = if (is_bernoulli) {
        min(mean_parameter[upper] * (1 - mean_parameter[upper]))
      } else NA_real_,
      global_min_expected_information = min(expected_information[upper]),
      global_min_worst_outcome_observed_curvature = min(
        worst_outcome_observed_curvature[upper]
      ),
      target_min_expected_information = min(target_information),
      target_min_worst_outcome_observed_curvature = min(
        worst_outcome_observed_curvature[config$target_node, target_other]
      ),
      oracle_node_information_eigenvalues = sort(
        eigen(
          oracle_node_information,
          symmetric = TRUE,
          only.values = TRUE
        )$values
      ),
      oracle_node_information_eigenvalues_per_n = sort(
        eigen(
          oracle_node_information,
          symmetric = TRUE,
          only.values = TRUE
        )$values
      ) / n,
      maximum_abs_theta = max(abs(Theta_star[upper])),
      analytical_theta_bound =
        maximum_row_norm^2 * lambda_operator_norm,
      probability_floor = config$probability_floor,
      curvature_floor = config$curvature_floor,
      node_information_floor = config$node_information_floor,
      truth_check_action = config$truth_check_action
    )
  )
}

# Always enforce construction identities and parameter-space bounds.
# truth_check_action controls only additional regularity thresholds:
# "error" stops, "warning" reports, and "none" records issues silently.
apply_truth_checks <- function(diagnostics, config, tolerance = 1e-8) {
  if (!is.null(diagnostics$raw_ball_radius_bound) &&
      diagnostics$raw_max_row_norm >
        diagnostics$raw_ball_radius_bound + tolerance) {
    stop("The raw uniform-ball row-norm bound failed.")
  }
  if (diagnostics$gram_max_abs_error > tolerance) {
    stop("Whitened U_star failed U_star^T U_star=nI_k.")
  }
  if (diagnostics$maximum_abs_theta >
      diagnostics$analytical_theta_bound + tolerance) {
    stop("The analytical bound on max |Theta_star| failed.")
  }
  if (diagnostics$maximum_row_norm > config$M_bound_U + tolerance) {
    stop(
      "The realized truth violates M_bound_U; increase M_bound_U."
    )
  }
  if (diagnostics$lambda_operator_norm >
      config$M_bound_Lambda + tolerance) {
    stop("The realized truth violates M_bound_Lambda.")
  }

  issues <- character()
  if (config$model %in% c("bernoulli_logit", "bernoulli_probit") &&
      !is.na(config$probability_floor)) {
    p_range <- diagnostics$global_probability_range
    if (p_range[1L] < config$probability_floor ||
        p_range[2L] > 1 - config$probability_floor) {
      issues <- c(issues, sprintf(
        paste0(
          "probability range [%.6g, %.6g] is outside ",
          "[%.6g, %.6g]"
        ),
        p_range[1L], p_range[2L], config$probability_floor,
        1 - config$probability_floor
      ))
    }
  }
  if (!is.na(config$curvature_floor)) {
    if (diagnostics$global_min_expected_information <
        config$curvature_floor) {
      issues <- c(issues, sprintf(
        "minimum expected Fisher %.6g is below %.6g",
        diagnostics$global_min_expected_information,
        config$curvature_floor
      ))
    }
    if (diagnostics$global_min_worst_outcome_observed_curvature <
        config$curvature_floor) {
      issues <- c(issues, sprintf(
        paste0(
          "minimum possible (worst-outcome) observed curvature ",
          "%.6g is below %.6g"
        ),
        diagnostics$global_min_worst_outcome_observed_curvature,
        config$curvature_floor
      ))
    }
  }
  if (!is.na(config$node_information_floor) &&
      min(diagnostics$oracle_node_information_eigenvalues_per_n) <
        config$node_information_floor) {
    issues <- c(issues, sprintf(
      paste0(
        "minimum oracle target-node information eigenvalue/n %.6g ",
        "is below %.6g"
      ),
      min(diagnostics$oracle_node_information_eigenvalues_per_n),
      config$node_information_floor
    ))
  }

  if (length(issues) && config$truth_check_action != "none") {
    message_text <- paste0(
      "Truth regularity check: ", paste(unique(issues), collapse = "; "),
      ". This is a property of the selected pilot setting, not an ",
      "estimation-code error."
    )
    if (config$truth_check_action == "error") stop(message_text)
    warning(message_text, call. = FALSE, immediate. = TRUE)
  }
  invisible(issues)
}

# Print the selected truth and its numerical regularity diagnostics.
print_truth_diagnostics <- function(diagnostics) {
  cat("\n================ Truth Diagnostics ================\n")
  cat("Model:", diagnostics$model, "\n")
  cat(sprintf(
    "n: %d; k: %d; Theorem 1 chi-square df: %d; Theorem 2 df: %d\n",
    diagnostics$n, diagnostics$k, diagnostics$k,
    diagnostics$k * (diagnostics$k + 1L) / 2L
  ))
  cat(
    "Lambda diagonal:",
    paste(format(diagnostics$lambda_values, digits = 8), collapse = ", "),
    "\n"
  )
  cat("Truth design:", diagnostics$truth_design, "\n")
  cat("Design seed:", diagnostics$design_seed, "\n")
  cat(sprintf(
    "Rejection sampling: %.0f batches, %.0f candidates, acceptance %.4f\n",
    diagnostics$rejection_batch_count,
    diagnostics$rejection_candidate_count,
    diagnostics$rejection_acceptance_rate
  ))
  cat(sprintf(
    paste0(
      "Raw ball radius bound: %.6f; realized raw max row norm: %.6f\n"
    ),
    diagnostics$raw_ball_radius_bound,
    diagnostics$raw_max_row_norm
  ))
  cat(
    "Raw row-norm quantiles (0%,25%,50%,75%,100%):",
    paste(sprintf("%.6f", diagnostics$raw_row_norm_quantiles),
          collapse = ", "),
    "\n"
  )
  cat(
    "Uncentered sample second-moment eigenvalues:",
    paste(sprintf("%.6f", diagnostics$sample_second_moment_eigenvalues),
          collapse = ", "),
    "\n"
  )
  cat(sprintf(
    "Sample second-moment condition number: %.6f\n",
    diagnostics$sample_second_moment_condition_number
  ))
  cat(sprintf(
    paste0(
      "After whitening: max row norm %.6f; max |column mean| %.3e; ",
      "max |U^T U-nI| %.3e (no centering constraint)\n"
    ),
    diagnostics$maximum_row_norm,
    diagnostics$whitened_max_abs_column_mean,
    diagnostics$gram_max_abs_error
  ))
  cat(sprintf(
    "Theta range: [%.6f, %.6f]; analytical max-|Theta| bound %.6f\n",
    diagnostics$global_theta_range[1L],
    diagnostics$global_theta_range[2L],
    diagnostics$analytical_theta_bound
  ))
  if (diagnostics$model %in% c("bernoulli_logit", "bernoulli_probit")) {
    cat(sprintf(
      "Probability range: [%.8g, %.8g]\n",
      diagnostics$global_probability_range[1L],
      diagnostics$global_probability_range[2L]
    ))
    cat(sprintf(
      "Minimum Bernoulli variance p(1-p): %.8g\n",
      diagnostics$global_min_bernoulli_variance
    ))
  } else {
    cat(sprintf(
      "Mean-parameter range: [%.8g, %.8g]\n",
      diagnostics$global_mean_parameter_range[1L],
      diagnostics$global_mean_parameter_range[2L]
    ))
  }
  cat(sprintf(
    paste0(
      "Minimum expected Fisher: %.8g; minimum possible ",
      "(worst-outcome) observed curvature: %.8g\n"
    ),
    diagnostics$global_min_expected_information,
    diagnostics$global_min_worst_outcome_observed_curvature
  ))
  cat(
    "Oracle target-node information eigenvalues / n:",
    paste(
      sprintf("%.8g", diagnostics$oracle_node_information_eigenvalues_per_n),
      collapse = ", "
    ),
    "\n"
  )
  if (!is.na(diagnostics$probability_floor)) {
    cat(sprintf(
      "Requested probability interval: [%.6g, %.6g]\n",
      diagnostics$probability_floor,
      1 - diagnostics$probability_floor
    ))
  }
  if (!is.na(diagnostics$curvature_floor)) {
    cat(sprintf(
      "Requested Fisher/worst-outcome-curvature floor: %.6g\n",
      diagnostics$curvature_floor
    ))
  }
  if (!is.na(diagnostics$node_information_floor)) {
    cat(sprintf(
      "Requested target-node information eigenvalue/n floor: %.6g\n",
      diagnostics$node_information_floor
    ))
  }
  if (length(diagnostics$regularity_issues)) {
    cat(
      "Regularity warnings:",
      paste(diagnostics$regularity_issues, collapse = "; "),
      "\n"
    )
  } else {
    cat("Regularity warnings: none\n")
  }
  cat("Truth check action:", diagnostics$truth_check_action, "\n")
  cat("===================================================\n")
  invisible(diagnostics)
}

# Construct one latent design, Lambda_star, and edge means shared by replications.
generate_truth <- function(config) {
  if (config$truth_design != "uniform_ball_rejection_whitened_no_centering") {
    stop("Unsupported truth_design: ", config$truth_design)
  }
  design <- generate_uniform_ball_rejection_whitened_no_centering_U(
    n = config$n,
    k = config$k,
    design_seed = config$design_seed,
    eigen_floor = config$whitening_eigen_floor
  )
  U_star <- design$U_star
  Lambda_star <- diag(config$lambda_vec, config$k, config$k)
  Theta_star <- U_star %*% Lambda_star %*% t(U_star)
  diag(Theta_star) <- 0
  mean_star <- link_probability(Theta_star, config)
  diag(mean_star) <- 0
  diagnostics <- calculate_truth_diagnostics(
    U_star, Lambda_star, Theta_star, config, design$diagnostics
  )
  diagnostics$regularity_issues <- apply_truth_checks(diagnostics, config)
  list(
    U_star = U_star,
    Lambda_star = Lambda_star,
    Theta_star = Theta_star,
    mean_star = mean_star,
    P_star = if (
      config$model %in% c("bernoulli_logit", "bernoulli_probit")
    ) mean_star else NULL,
    design_seed = config$design_seed,
    diagnostics = diagnostics
  )
}

# Draw independent upper-triangle edges conditional on truth, then mirror them.
generate_network_rep <- function(truth, config, replication_seed) {
  set_reproducible_seed(replication_seed)
  n <- config$n
  upper <- upper.tri(matrix(0, n, n), diag = FALSE)
  theta <- truth$Theta_star[upper]
  mean_parameter <- truth$mean_star[upper]
  values <- switch(
    config$model,
    bernoulli_logit = as.numeric(
      runif(length(theta)) < mean_parameter
    ),
    bernoulli_probit = as.numeric(
      runif(length(theta)) < mean_parameter
    ),
    gaussian = theta + rnorm(length(theta), 0, config$sigma),
    poisson = rpois(length(theta), mean_parameter)
  )
  A <- matrix(0, n, n)
  A[upper] <- values
  A <- A + t(A)
  diag(A) <- 0
  A
}

# -------------------- Spectral initialization -------------------

# Select singular directions above the initialization threshold, keeping >= K.
spectral_keep_indices <- function(singular_values, k, offset) {
  p <- length(singular_values)
  threshold_index <- k + offset + 1L
  threshold <- if (threshold_index <= p) {
    singular_values[threshold_index] + 1e-6
  } else {
    0
  }
  keep <- which(singular_values > threshold)
  if (length(keep) < k) keep <- seq_len(min(k, p))
  keep
}

# Initialize U and Lambda from a model-specific transformed spectral estimate.
initialize_spectral <- function(A, config) {
  n <- nrow(A)
  k <- config$k
  sv <- svd(A)

  if (config$model %in% c("bernoulli_logit", "bernoulli_probit")) {
    keep <- spectral_keep_indices(sv$d, k, offset = 2L)
    P_tilde <- sv$u[, keep, drop = FALSE] %*%
      diag(sv$d[keep], length(keep)) %*% t(sv$v[, keep, drop = FALSE])
    P_tilde <- pmax(
      pmin(symmetrize(P_tilde), 1 - config$probability_eps),
      config$probability_eps
    )
    Theta_tilde <- symmetrize(link_inverse(P_tilde, config))
  } else if (config$model == "gaussian") {
    keep <- spectral_keep_indices(sv$d, k, offset = 0L)
    Theta_tilde <- sv$u[, keep, drop = FALSE] %*%
      diag(sv$d[keep], length(keep)) %*% t(sv$v[, keep, drop = FALSE])
    Theta_tilde <- symmetrize(Theta_tilde)
  } else {
    keep <- spectral_keep_indices(sv$d, k, offset = 2L)
    intensity_tilde <- sv$u[, keep, drop = FALSE] %*%
      diag(sv$d[keep], length(keep)) %*% t(sv$v[, keep, drop = FALSE])
    intensity_tilde <- pmax(symmetrize(intensity_tilde), 0.1)
    Theta_tilde <- symmetrize(log(intensity_tilde))
  }

  diag(Theta_tilde) <- 0
  eg <- eigen(Theta_tilde, symmetric = TRUE)
  idx <- order(abs(eg$values), decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(k)]
  list(
    U_init = sqrt(n) * eg$vectors[, idx, drop = FALSE],
    Lambda_init = diag(eg$values[idx] / n, k, k)
  )
}

# -------------------- Objective, gradient, PGD ------------------

# Evaluate the network objective using each off-diagonal edge exactly once.
calculate_objective_network <- function(U, Lambda, A, config) {
  Theta <- U %*% Lambda %*% t(U)
  diag(Theta) <- 0
  upper <- upper.tri(A, diag = FALSE)
  negative_loglikelihood_edges(Theta[upper], A[upper], config)
}

# Assemble U and symmetric-Lambda update gradients, excluding diagonal entries.
calculate_gradient_network <- function(U, Lambda, A, config) {
  Theta <- U %*% Lambda %*% t(U)
  diag(Theta) <- 0
  D <- negative_score_matrix(Theta, A, config)
  diag(D) <- 0
  grad_Lambda <- 0.5 * t(U) %*% D %*% U
  list(
    grad_U = D %*% U %*% Lambda,
    grad_Lambda = symmetrize(grad_Lambda)
  )
}

# Fit one network by projected gradient descent and return diagnostics.
# max_iter and n_iter count optimizer updates for this network; n_sim
# instead counts networks in the outer Monte Carlo loop. Convergence
# uses the scaled projected residual, not objective change or a p-value.
run_pgd_network <- function(A, config) {
  n <- config$n
  init <- initialize_spectral(A, config)
  U_projection <- project_C_U_certified(
    init$U_init, config$M_bound_U, context = "spectral initialization"
  )
  U_hat <- U_projection$U
  Lambda_hat <- proximal_projection_Lambda(
    init$Lambda_init, config$M_bound_Lambda
  )

  convergence_code <- 1L
  scaled_gradient <- Inf
  projected_residual_U <- Inf
  projected_residual_Lambda_v <- Inf
  iter_done <- 0L
  projection_calls <- 1L
  projection_max_row_ratio <- U_projection$max_row_ratio
  projection_min_row_margin <- U_projection$row_margin
  projection_max_gram_error <- U_projection$gram_error
  projection_max_objective_gap <- U_projection$objective_gap

  for (iter in seq_len(config$max_iter)) {
    grads <- calculate_gradient_network(U_hat, Lambda_hat, A, config)
    U_projection <- project_C_U_certified(
      U_hat - config$learning_rate * grads$grad_U / n,
      config$M_bound_U, context = sprintf("PGD iteration %d", iter)
    )
    U_next <- U_projection$U
    projection_calls <- projection_calls + 1L
    projection_max_row_ratio <- max(
      projection_max_row_ratio, U_projection$max_row_ratio
    )
    projection_min_row_margin <- min(
      projection_min_row_margin, U_projection$row_margin
    )
    projection_max_gram_error <- max(
      projection_max_gram_error, U_projection$gram_error
    )
    projection_max_objective_gap <- max(
      projection_max_objective_gap, U_projection$objective_gap
    )
    Lambda_next <- proximal_projection_Lambda(
      Lambda_hat - config$learning_rate * grads$grad_Lambda / n^2,
      config$M_bound_Lambda
    )

    # On the orthogonality-constrained parameter space, the raw Euclidean
    # gradient need not vanish at the optimum. The mapping must be divided by
    # the effective steps actually used by the code: eta_U = lr/n and, under
    # the paper's lambda_v parameterization, eta_lambda_v = lr/(2 n^2).
    residuals <- projected_gradient_mapping_components(
      U_hat, U_next, Lambda_hat, Lambda_next,
      config$learning_rate, n
    )
    projected_residual_U <- residuals[["U"]]
    projected_residual_Lambda_v <- residuals[["Lambda_v"]]
    scaled_gradient <- max(residuals)
    if (!is.finite(scaled_gradient)) {
      convergence_code <- 2L
      break
    }
    U_hat <- U_next
    Lambda_hat <- Lambda_next
    iter_done <- iter
    if (scaled_gradient < config$tolerance) {
      convergence_code <- 0L
      break
    }
  }

  # The final update can itself cross the tolerance. Re-evaluate at the
  # returned iterate so a max-iteration exit is classified correctly.
  if (convergence_code == 1L) {
    final_grads <- calculate_gradient_network(U_hat, Lambda_hat, A, config)
    final_U_projection <- project_C_U_certified(
      U_hat - config$learning_rate * final_grads$grad_U / n,
      config$M_bound_U, context = "final residual check"
    )
    final_U_next <- final_U_projection$U
    projection_calls <- projection_calls + 1L
    projection_max_row_ratio <- max(
      projection_max_row_ratio, final_U_projection$max_row_ratio
    )
    projection_min_row_margin <- min(
      projection_min_row_margin, final_U_projection$row_margin
    )
    projection_max_gram_error <- max(
      projection_max_gram_error, final_U_projection$gram_error
    )
    projection_max_objective_gap <- max(
      projection_max_objective_gap, final_U_projection$objective_gap
    )
    final_Lambda_next <- proximal_projection_Lambda(
      Lambda_hat -
        config$learning_rate * final_grads$grad_Lambda / n^2,
      config$M_bound_Lambda
    )
    final_residuals <- projected_gradient_mapping_components(
      U_hat, final_U_next, Lambda_hat, final_Lambda_next,
      config$learning_rate, n
    )
    projected_residual_U <- final_residuals[["U"]]
    projected_residual_Lambda_v <- final_residuals[["Lambda_v"]]
    scaled_gradient <- max(final_residuals)
    if (!is.finite(scaled_gradient)) {
      convergence_code <- 2L
    } else if (scaled_gradient < config$tolerance) {
      convergence_code <- 0L
    }
  }

  final_objective <- calculate_objective_network(U_hat, Lambda_hat, A, config)
  if (!is.finite(final_objective)) convergence_code <- 2L
  list(
    U_hat = U_hat,
    Lambda_hat = symmetrize(Lambda_hat),
    convergence_code = convergence_code,
    n_iter = iter_done,
    scaled_gradient = scaled_gradient,
    projected_residual_U = projected_residual_U,
    projected_residual_Lambda_v = projected_residual_Lambda_v,
    projection_calls = projection_calls,
    projection_max_row_ratio = projection_max_row_ratio,
    projection_min_row_margin = projection_min_row_margin,
    projection_max_gram_error = projection_max_gram_error,
    projection_max_objective_gap = projection_max_objective_gap,
    final_objective = final_objective
  )
}

# ---------------- Rotation and node-wise inference ---------------

# Align the fitted latent basis to U_star by orthogonal Procrustes rotation.
# Rotate Lambda consistently so fitted edge predictors remain unchanged.
# This oracle alignment requires known truth and is unavailable in real data.
rotate_estimator <- function(U_hat, Lambda_hat, U_star) {
  n <- nrow(U_hat)
  if (nrow(U_star) != n || ncol(U_hat) != ncol(U_star)) {
    stop("U_hat and U_star must have identical dimensions for rotation.")
  }
  alignment_cross_gram <- crossprod(U_hat, U_star) / n
  sv <- svd(alignment_cross_gram)
  Q_transpose <- sv$u %*% t(sv$v)
  min_sv <- min(sv$d)
  max_sv <- max(sv$d)
  condition_number <- if (
    is.finite(min_sv) && min_sv > .Machine$double.eps * max_sv
  ) max_sv / min_sv else Inf
  list(
    U_q = U_hat %*% Q_transpose,
    Lambda_q = symmetrize(t(Q_transpose) %*% Lambda_hat %*% Q_transpose),
    Q_transpose = Q_transpose,
    alignment_min_singular_value = min_sv,
    alignment_condition_number = condition_number
  )
}

# Compute the fitted observed-information matrix for one node's K coordinates.
calculate_node_information <- function(U, Lambda, node_idx, config, A = NULL) {
  Theta <- U %*% Lambda %*% t(U)
  diag(Theta) <- 0
  # Use the realized negative Hessian for Theorem 1 standardization.
  # For Gaussian, logit, and Poisson it equals expected Fisher information;
  # for probit it also depends on the observed edge outcomes in A.
  V <- observed_information_matrix(Theta, config, A)
  diag(V) <- 0
  W <- U %*% Lambda
  symmetrize(t(W) %*% (V[node_idx, ] * W))
}

# --------------- Constrained joint information ------------------

# Build constraint derivatives, using U_anchor for the rotational constraints.
build_D_UG <- function(U, U_anchor) {
  n <- nrow(U)
  k <- ncol(U)
  if (!identical(dim(U_anchor), dim(U))) {
    stop("U and U_anchor must have identical dimensions in build_D_UG().")
  }
  DUG <- matrix(0, n * k, k^2)

  for (a in seq_len(k)) {
    DUG[seq(a, n * k, by = k), a] <- U[, a]
  }

  pair <- 1L
  if (k >= 2L) {
    for (a in seq_len(k - 1L)) {
      for (b in seq.int(a + 1L, k)) {
        col_g2 <- k + pair
        col_g3 <- k + k * (k - 1L) / 2L + pair
        rows_a <- seq(a, n * k, by = k)
        rows_b <- seq(b, n * k, by = k)
        DUG[rows_a, col_g2] <- U[, b] / sqrt(2)
        DUG[rows_b, col_g2] <- U[, a] / sqrt(2)
        DUG[rows_a, col_g3] <- U_anchor[, b] / sqrt(2)
        DUG[rows_b, col_g3] <- -U_anchor[, a] / sqrt(2)
        pair <- pair + 1L
      }
    }
  }

  if (any(!is.finite(DUG))) stop("D_UG contains non-finite entries.")
  DUG
}

# Form joint information from observed edge curvature and predictor derivatives.
# Project out constrained U directions to obtain efficient Lambda information.
# Retain expected node blocks separately for the B1/BM/BP bias formulas.
build_information_blocks <- function(U, Lambda, U_anchor, config, A = NULL) {
  n <- nrow(U)
  k <- ncol(U)
  d <- k * (k + 1L) / 2L
  Theta <- U %*% Lambda %*% t(U)
  diag(Theta) <- 0
  # Weight the joint information blocks by observed edge curvature. Probit
  # uses the observed outcomes; the other models agree with Fisher weights.
  V <- observed_information_matrix(Theta, config, A)
  V_expected <- expected_derivative_terms(Theta, config)$information
  diag(V) <- 0
  diag(V_expected) <- 0
  W <- U %*% Lambda

  SUU <- matrix(0, n * k, n * k)
  SUL <- matrix(0, n * k, d)
  SLL <- matrix(0, d, d)
  expected_blocks <- lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) matrix(0, k, k))

  for (i in seq_len(n - 1L)) {
    ii <- ((i - 1L) * k + 1L):(i * k)
    for (j in seq.int(i + 1L, n)) {
      jj <- ((j - 1L) * k + 1L):(j * k)
      v <- V[i, j]
      v_expected <- V_expected[i, j]
      wi <- W[i, ]
      wj <- W[j, ]
      ld <- lambda_direction_derivative(U[i, ], U[j, ])

      SUU[ii, ii] <- SUU[ii, ii] + v * tcrossprod(wj)
      SUU[jj, jj] <- SUU[jj, jj] + v * tcrossprod(wi)
      cross <- v * tcrossprod(wj, wi)
      SUU[ii, jj] <- SUU[ii, jj] + cross
      SUU[jj, ii] <- SUU[jj, ii] + t(cross)
      SUL[ii, ] <- SUL[ii, ] + v * tcrossprod(wj, ld)
      SUL[jj, ] <- SUL[jj, ] + v * tcrossprod(wi, ld)
      SLL <- SLL + v * tcrossprod(ld)
      expected_blocks[[i]] <- expected_blocks[[i]] +
        v_expected * tcrossprod(wj)
      expected_blocks[[j]] <- expected_blocks[[j]] +
        v_expected * tcrossprod(wi)
    }
  }

  SUU <- symmetrize(SUU)
  SLL <- symmetrize(SLL)
  SLU <- t(SUL)
  DUG <- build_D_UG(U, U_anchor)
  DGU <- t(DUG)
  DGU_DUG <- symmetrize(DGU %*% DUG)
  DGU_DUG_inverse <- ordinary_inverse_pd(
    DGU_DUG, "D_GU D_UG nuisance Gram matrix"
  )
  # Finite-sample nuisance projector. Do not replace D_GU D_UG by n I:
  # Pi_nui = D_UG (D_GU D_UG)^+ D_GU. The numerical-rank check above makes
  # the Moore-Penrose inverse equal to the ordinary inverse used here.
  Pi_nui <- symmetrize(
    DUG %*% DGU_DUG_inverse$inverse %*% DGU
  )
  PUU <- symmetrize(diag(n * k) - Pi_nui)
  PUU_idempotence_error <- max(abs(PUU %*% PUU - PUU))
  PUU_DUG_annihilation_error <- max(abs(PUU %*% DUG))
  if (PUU_idempotence_error > 1e-8 ||
      PUU_DUG_annihilation_error > 1e-8 * max(1, max(abs(DUG)))) {
    stop(sprintf(
      paste0(
        "Failed to construct the finite-sample nuisance projector: ",
        "idempotence error %.4e, annihilation error %.4e."
      ),
      PUU_idempotence_error, PUU_DUG_annihilation_error
    ))
  }
  projected <- symmetrize(PUU %*% SUU %*% PUU)
  projected_inv <- safe_pinv_psd(projected, n_drop = k^2)
  Seff <- symmetrize(
    SLL - SLU %*% PUU %*% projected_inv %*% PUU %*% SUL
  )

  blocks <- lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    idx <- ((i - 1L) * k + 1L):(i * k)
    SUU[idx, idx, drop = FALSE]
  })

  list(
    SUU = SUU, SUL = SUL, SLU = SLU, SLL = SLL,
    DUG = DUG, DGU = DGU,
    DGU_DUG = DGU_DUG,
    DGU_DUG_inverse = DGU_DUG_inverse$inverse,
    DUG_gram_error_from_nI = max(abs(DGU_DUG / n - diag(k^2))),
    DUG_gram_condition_number = DGU_DUG_inverse$condition_number,
    Pi_nui = Pi_nui, PUU = PUU,
    PUU_idempotence_error = PUU_idempotence_error,
    PUU_DUG_annihilation_error = PUU_DUG_annihilation_error,
    projected_inv = projected_inv,
    Seff = Seff, blocks = blocks, expected_blocks = expected_blocks
  )
}

# ------------------ Bias and debiasing terms --------------------

# Compute B1, BM, and BP terms using expected node information and edge moments.
calculate_bias_terms <- function(U, Lambda, expected_blocks, config) {
  n <- nrow(U)
  k <- ncol(U)
  d <- k * (k + 1L) / 2L
  Theta <- U %*% Lambda %*% t(U)
  diag(Theta) <- 0
  terms <- expected_derivative_terms(Theta, config)
  W <- U %*% Lambda
  inv_blocks <- lapply(expected_blocks, safe_pinv_psd)
  inverse_sum <- Reduce(`+`, inv_blocks)

  B1U <- numeric(n * k)
  B1L <- numeric(d)
  BMU <- numeric(n * k)
  BML <- numeric(d)
  BPU_matrix <- 0.5 * U %*% t(inverse_sum)

  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    idx_i <- ((i - 1L) * k + 1L):(i * k)
    wi <- matrix(W[i, ], k, 1L)
    b1_i <- matrix(0, k, 1L)
    bm_i <- matrix(0, k, 1L)

    for (j in setdiff(seq_len(n), i)) {
      wj <- matrix(W[j, ], k, 1L)
      ld <- lambda_direction_derivative(U[i, ], U[j, ])
      q_i_j <- as.numeric(t(wi) %*% inv_blocks[[j]] %*% wi)
      q_j_i <- as.numeric(t(wj) %*% inv_blocks[[i]] %*% wj)
      e3 <- terms$expected_ell3[i, j]
      em <- terms$expected_score_ell2[i, j]

      b1_i <- b1_i - 0.5 * e3 * (q_i_j + q_j_i) * wj
      bm_i <- bm_i + em * (q_i_j + q_j_i) * wj
      B1L <- B1L - 0.5 * e3 * q_i_j * ld
      BML <- BML + em * q_i_j * ld
    }
    B1U[idx_i] <- as.vector(b1_i)
    BMU[idx_i] <- as.vector(bm_i)
  }

  list(
    B1U = B1U, B1L = B1L,
    BMU = BMU, BML = BML,
    BPU = as.vector(t(BPU_matrix))
  )
}

# Compute likelihood and constraint-penalty corrections in lambda_v units.
# The corrected estimate is lambda_v_hat + correction_total (ADDITIVE).
# correction_penalty already includes its minus sign.
# U_star is the known-truth anchor used for this simulation convention.
calculate_debiasing_components <- function(
  U, Lambda, U_star, config, A = NULL
) {
  n <- nrow(U)
  info <- build_information_blocks(U, Lambda, U_star, config, A = A)
  SLL_inverse <- ordinary_inverse_pd(
    info$SLL, "Theorem 2 Lambda information"
  )
  Seff_inverse <- ordinary_inverse_pd(
    info$Seff, "Theorem 2 efficient information"
  )
  # The B1/BM/BP formulas use the expected node-information blocks; keep
  # those separate from the observed Hessian blocks used in Seff above.
  bias <- calculate_bias_terms(U, Lambda, info$expected_blocks, config)

  core <- (bias$B1L - bias$BML) -
    info$SLU %*% info$PUU %*% info$projected_inv %*% info$PUU %*%
    (bias$B1U - bias$BMU)

  correction_likelihood <- as.vector(
    Seff_inverse$inverse %*% core
  )
  penalty_direction <- info$DUG %*% crossprod(info$DUG, bias$BPU)
  correction_penalty <- -as.vector(
    SLL_inverse$inverse %*% info$SLU %*%
      penalty_direction / n^2
  )

  list(
    Seff = info$Seff,
    lambda_v_hat = get_lambda_v(Lambda),
    correction_likelihood = correction_likelihood,
    correction_penalty = correction_penalty,
    correction_total = correction_likelihood + correction_penalty,
    max_abs_BM = max(abs(c(bias$BMU, bias$BML))),
    DUG_gram_error_from_nI = info$DUG_gram_error_from_nI,
    DUG_gram_condition_number = info$DUG_gram_condition_number,
    PUU_idempotence_error = info$PUU_idempotence_error,
    PUU_DUG_annihilation_error = info$PUU_DUG_annihilation_error,
    SLL_min_eigenvalue = SLL_inverse$min_eigenvalue,
    SLL_condition_number = SLL_inverse$condition_number,
    SLL_inverse_residual = SLL_inverse$inverse_residual,
    Seff_min_eigenvalue = Seff_inverse$min_eigenvalue,
    Seff_condition_number = Seff_inverse$condition_number,
    Seff_inverse_residual = Seff_inverse$inverse_residual
  )
}

# --------------------- Monte Carlo replication ------------------

# Define one CSV row per attempted replication, with K-dependent columns.
# stat_U_*: standardized errors for target_node; chi_sq_U: their squared norm.
# raw_lambda_* / debiased_lambda_*: standardized errors, not estimates.
# lambda_raw_error_* / lambda_debiased_error_*: errors in lambda_v units.
# correction_likelihood_* / correction_penalty_*: additive corrections
# in those same units. Diagnostics and failed rows are retained.
result_column_names <- function(k) {
  d <- k * (k + 1L) / 2L
  names <- c(
    paste0("stat_U_", seq_len(k)),
    "chi_sq_U", "chi_sq_debiased_lambda",
    "convergence_code", "n_iter", "scaled_gradient",
    "projected_residual_U", "projected_residual_Lambda_v",
    "projection_calls", "projection_max_row_ratio",
    "projection_min_row_margin", "projection_max_gram_error",
    "projection_max_objective_gap",
    "final_objective", "alignment_min_singular_value",
    "alignment_condition_number", "max_abs_BM",
    "DUG_gram_error_from_nI", "DUG_gram_condition_number",
    "PUU_idempotence_error", "PUU_DUG_annihilation_error",
    "SLL_min_eigenvalue", "SLL_condition_number", "SLL_inverse_residual",
    "Seff_min_eigenvalue", "Seff_condition_number", "Seff_inverse_residual"
  )
  for (i in seq_len(d)) {
    names <- c(
      names,
      paste0("raw_lambda_", i),
      paste0("debiased_lambda_", i),
      paste0("lambda_raw_error_", i),
      paste0("lambda_debiased_error_", i),
      paste0("correction_likelihood_", i),
      paste0("correction_penalty_", i)
    )
  }
  names
}

# Create an NA row retaining the status: 1 = iteration limit, 2 = non-finite
# optimizer result, 3 = a caught fitting or inference error. Code 0 denotes
# successful completion in one_replication(). An uncertified U projection
# instead aborts the full run; see the active_U_row_bound handler below.
failed_result <- function(k, code = 3L) {
  out <- rep(NA_real_, length(result_column_names(k)))
  names(out) <- result_column_names(k)
  out["convergence_code"] <- code
  out
}

# Simulate, fit, align, and standardize one network under the fixed latent truth.
one_replication <- function(sim, truth, config) {
  k <- config$k
  pgd_diagnostic_names <- c(
    "n_iter", "scaled_gradient",
    "projected_residual_U", "projected_residual_Lambda_v",
    "projection_calls", "projection_max_row_ratio",
    "projection_min_row_margin", "projection_max_gram_error",
    "projection_max_objective_gap", "final_objective"
  )
  tryCatch({
    A <- generate_network_rep(
      truth,
      config,
      config$replication_seed_base + sim
    )
    fit <- run_pgd_network(A, config)
    if (fit$convergence_code != 0L) {
      out <- failed_result(k, fit$convergence_code)
      out[pgd_diagnostic_names] <- unlist(
        fit[pgd_diagnostic_names], use.names = FALSE
      )
      return(out)
    }

    rot <- rotate_estimator(fit$U_hat, fit$Lambda_hat, truth$U_star)
    node_info <- calculate_node_information(
      rot$U_q, rot$Lambda_q, config$target_node, config, A = A
    )
    assert_positive_definite(node_info, "Theorem 1 node information")
    # Theorem 1: z_U = node_info^(1/2) (u_hat_aligned - u_star),
    # with K components for the selected node. node_info already sums edge
    # contributions, so no extra sqrt(n) factor is applied. The matrix square root
    # standardizes the full vector and can mix its original coordinates.
    z_U <- as.vector(
      safe_sqrt_psd(node_info) %*%
        (rot$U_q[config$target_node, ] - truth$U_star[config$target_node, ])
    )

    # Theorem 2 uses the full-network information and does not depend on
    # target_node. Retain U_star as the oracle rotational-constraint anchor.
    deb <- calculate_debiasing_components(
      rot$U_q, rot$Lambda_q, truth$U_star, config, A = A
    )
    true_v <- get_lambda_v(truth$Lambda_star)
    raw_v <- deb$lambda_v_hat
    corrected_v <- raw_v + deb$correction_total
    Seff_half <- safe_sqrt_psd(deb$Seff)
    # Apply the same efficient-information square root before and after
    # correction. These d-dimensional standardized components may mix
    # the original lambda_v coordinates; they are not Lambda entries.
    z_raw <- as.vector(Seff_half %*% (raw_v - true_v))
    z_debiased <- as.vector(Seff_half %*% (corrected_v - true_v))

    out <- setNames(
      rep(NA_real_, length(result_column_names(k))),
      result_column_names(k)
    )
    out[paste0("stat_U_", seq_along(z_U))] <- z_U
    out[c(
      "chi_sq_U", "chi_sq_debiased_lambda",
      "convergence_code", "n_iter", "scaled_gradient",
      "projected_residual_U", "projected_residual_Lambda_v",
      "projection_calls", "projection_max_row_ratio",
      "projection_min_row_margin", "projection_max_gram_error",
      "projection_max_objective_gap",
      "final_objective", "alignment_min_singular_value",
      "alignment_condition_number", "max_abs_BM",
      "DUG_gram_error_from_nI", "DUG_gram_condition_number",
      "PUU_idempotence_error", "PUU_DUG_annihilation_error",
      "SLL_min_eigenvalue", "SLL_condition_number", "SLL_inverse_residual",
      "Seff_min_eigenvalue", "Seff_condition_number", "Seff_inverse_residual"
    )] <- c(
      sum(z_U^2), sum(z_debiased^2),
      fit$convergence_code, fit$n_iter, fit$scaled_gradient,
      fit$projected_residual_U, fit$projected_residual_Lambda_v,
      fit$projection_calls, fit$projection_max_row_ratio,
      fit$projection_min_row_margin, fit$projection_max_gram_error,
      fit$projection_max_objective_gap,
      fit$final_objective, rot$alignment_min_singular_value,
      rot$alignment_condition_number, deb$max_abs_BM,
      deb$DUG_gram_error_from_nI, deb$DUG_gram_condition_number,
      deb$PUU_idempotence_error, deb$PUU_DUG_annihilation_error,
      deb$SLL_min_eigenvalue, deb$SLL_condition_number,
      deb$SLL_inverse_residual,
      deb$Seff_min_eigenvalue, deb$Seff_condition_number,
      deb$Seff_inverse_residual
    )

    for (i in seq_along(raw_v)) {
      out[paste0("raw_lambda_", i)] <- z_raw[i]
      out[paste0("debiased_lambda_", i)] <- z_debiased[i]
      out[paste0("lambda_raw_error_", i)] <- raw_v[i] - true_v[i]
      out[paste0("lambda_debiased_error_", i)] <- corrected_v[i] - true_v[i]
      out[paste0("correction_likelihood_", i)] <-
        deb$correction_likelihood[i]
      out[paste0("correction_penalty_", i)] <-
        deb$correction_penalty[i]
    }
    out
  }, error = function(e) {
    if (inherits(e, "active_U_row_bound")) {
      # This event invalidates the exact-projection claim. Abort the full
      # formal run rather than silently excluding the affected replication.
      stop(e)
    }
    message("Replication ", sim, " failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    failed_result(k, 3L)
  })
}

# Run conditional Monte Carlo replications with reproducible seeds and <= 7 workers.
run_monte_carlo <- function(config, n_cores = NULL, truth = NULL) {
  validate_model_config(config)
  if (is.null(truth)) truth <- generate_truth(config)
  required_truth_fields <- c(
    "U_star", "Lambda_star", "Theta_star", "mean_star", "diagnostics"
  )
  expected_U_dimension <- c(config$n, config$k)
  expected_Lambda_dimension <- c(config$k, config$k)
  expected_network_dimension <- c(config$n, config$n)
  if (!is.list(truth) ||
      !all(required_truth_fields %in% names(truth)) ||
      !identical(dim(truth$U_star), expected_U_dimension) ||
      !identical(dim(truth$Lambda_star), expected_Lambda_dimension) ||
      !identical(dim(truth$Theta_star), expected_network_dimension) ||
      !identical(dim(truth$mean_star), expected_network_dimension) ||
      !identical(truth$diagnostics$model, config$model) ||
      !identical(as.integer(truth$diagnostics$n), config$n) ||
      !identical(as.integer(truth$diagnostics$k), config$k) ||
      !identical(truth$diagnostics$truth_design, config$truth_design) ||
      !identical(
        as.integer(truth$diagnostics$design_seed), config$design_seed
      ) ||
      any(!is.finite(c(
        truth$U_star, truth$Lambda_star,
        truth$Theta_star, truth$mean_star
      ))) ||
      max(abs(
        truth$Lambda_star -
          diag(config$lambda_vec, config$k, config$k)
      )) > 1e-10) {
    stop("The supplied truth is incompatible with config.")
  }
  reconstructed_theta <- truth$U_star %*% truth$Lambda_star %*%
    t(truth$U_star)
  diag(reconstructed_theta) <- 0
  reconstructed_mean <- link_probability(reconstructed_theta, config)
  diag(reconstructed_mean) <- 0
  if (max(abs(truth$Theta_star - reconstructed_theta)) > 1e-8 ||
      max(abs(truth$mean_star - reconstructed_mean)) > 1e-8) {
    stop("The supplied truth matrices are internally inconsistent.")
  }
  print_truth_diagnostics(truth$diagnostics)
  if (is.null(n_cores)) {
    detected_cores <- suppressWarnings(parallel::detectCores())
    if (length(detected_cores) != 1L || !is.finite(detected_cores)) {
      detected_cores <- 1L
    }
    n_cores <- max(1L, as.integer(detected_cores) - 2L)
  } else if (length(n_cores) != 1L || !is.finite(n_cores) ||
             n_cores < 1L || n_cores != floor(n_cores)) {
    stop("n_cores must be a positive integer.")
  }
  n_cores <- max(1L, min(7L, as.integer(n_cores), as.integer(config$n_sim)))

  dense_dimension <- config$n * config$k
  one_dense_matrix_gb <- 8 * dense_dimension^2 / 1024^3
  estimated_dense_gb_per_worker <- 8 * one_dense_matrix_gb
  estimated_dense_gb_all_workers <-
    n_cores * estimated_dense_gb_per_worker
  if (dense_dimension >= 1600L || estimated_dense_gb_all_workers >= 2) {
    warning(
      sprintf(
        paste0(
          "Theorem 2 uses several dense (n*k)-by-(n*k) matrices per ",
          "worker (dimension %d). A rough lower-order estimate is %.3f GB ",
          "per worker and %.3f GB across %d workers; matrix products and R ",
          "copies require additional memory. Reduce n_cores or use separate ",
          "CHTC jobs if needed."
        ),
        dense_dimension, estimated_dense_gb_per_worker,
        estimated_dense_gb_all_workers, n_cores
      ),
      call. = FALSE,
      immediate. = TRUE
    )
  }

  cl <- NULL
  if (n_cores == 1L) {
    registerDoSEQ()
  } else {
    cl <- makeCluster(n_cores)
    registerDoParallel(cl)
    on.exit(try(stopCluster(cl), silent = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  }

  export_names <- c(
    "normalize_model_name", "validate_model_config",
    "set_reproducible_seed", "symmetrize", "sigmoid", "stable_log1pexp",
    "safe_pinv_psd", "safe_sqrt_psd", "assert_positive_definite",
    "ordinary_inverse_pd",
    "get_lambda_v",
    "lambda_direction_derivative", "project_C_U_certified",
    "proximal_projection_Lambda", "projected_gradient_mapping_components",
    "probit_ratios",
    "observed_information_matrix",
    "link_probability", "link_inverse", "negative_loglikelihood_edges",
    "negative_score_matrix", "expected_derivative_terms",
    "generate_network_rep", "spectral_keep_indices",
    "initialize_spectral", "calculate_objective_network",
    "calculate_gradient_network", "run_pgd_network",
    "rotate_estimator", "calculate_node_information",
    "build_D_UG", "build_information_blocks", "calculate_bias_terms",
    "calculate_debiasing_components", "result_column_names",
    "failed_result", "one_replication"
  )

  cat(sprintf(
    paste0(
      "Running %s: n=%d, k=%d, reps=%d, cores=%d, ",
      "lr=%g, max_iter=%d, tol=%g\n"
    ),
    config$model, config$n, config$k, config$n_sim, n_cores,
    config$learning_rate, config$max_iter, config$tolerance
  ))

  results <- foreach(
    sim = seq_len(config$n_sim),
    .combine = "rbind",
    .errorhandling = "stop",
    .export = export_names
  ) %dopar% one_replication(sim, truth, config)

  if (is.null(dim(results))) {
    result_names <- names(results)
    results <- matrix(
      as.numeric(results), nrow = 1L,
      dimnames = list(NULL, result_names)
    )
  } else {
    results <- as.matrix(results)
  }
  expected_names <- result_column_names(config$k)
  if (!identical(colnames(results), expected_names)) {
    stop("Internal result-column mismatch across replications.")
  }
  attr(results, "truth") <- truth
  attr(results, "config") <- config
  attr(results, "settings") <- list(
    config = config,
    truth_diagnostics = truth$diagnostics,
    convergence_metric = paste0(
      "max(||Delta_U||_max/(learning_rate/n), ",
      "||Delta_lambda_v||_inf/(learning_rate/(2*n^2)))"
    ),
    U_projection = paste0(
      "certified scaled-polar projection onto C_U; abort if the ",
      "M_bound_U row constraint is active"
    ),
    nuisance_projector = paste0(
      "P_UU = I - D_UG (D_GU D_UG)^+ D_GU; do not replace ",
      "the finite-sample D_GU D_UG by n I"
    ),
    penalty_DUG = "use the same theoretical D_UG D_GU product / n^2",
    memory_estimate = list(
      dense_dimension = dense_dimension,
      one_dense_matrix_gb = one_dense_matrix_gb,
      estimated_dense_gb_per_worker = estimated_dense_gb_per_worker,
      estimated_dense_gb_all_workers = estimated_dense_gb_all_workers
    ),
    rng_kind = c(
      kind = "Mersenne-Twister",
      normal.kind = "Inversion",
      sample.kind = "Rejection"
    ),
    n_cores = n_cores
  )
  cat("Finished.\n")
  results
}

# ---------------------- Summaries and plots ---------------------

# Exclude non-finite values before computing summaries or plotting quantiles.
finite_values <- function(x) x[is.finite(x)]

# By default select code-0 rows; plotting additionally removes non-finite values.
# Returning all rows does not reconstruct statistics missing after a failure.
inference_rows <- function(results, converged_only = TRUE) {
  if (!converged_only) return(seq_len(nrow(results)))
  which(results[, "convergence_code"] == 0)
}

# Compare one standardized component to N(0,1) across retained replications.
# The title reports mean(x) and sample SD sd(x), not variance or the
# Monte Carlo standard error of the mean. The reference line is y = x.
qqplot_standard_normal <- function(x, main, col = "darkblue") {
  x <- finite_values(x)
  if (length(x) < 2L) {
    plot.new()
    title(main = paste0(main, "\nInsufficient finite values"))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  qqnorm(
    x,
    main = sprintf("%s\nmean=%.4f, sd=%.4f", main, mean(x), sd(x)),
    pch = 20,
    col = col
  )
  abline(0, 1, col = "red", lwd = 2)
  invisible(NULL)
}

# Compare squared-norm statistics to their specified chi-square reference law.
qqplot_chisq <- function(x, df, main) {
  x <- sort(finite_values(x))
  if (length(x) < 2L) {
    plot.new()
    title(main = paste0(main, "\nInsufficient finite values"))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  plot(
    qchisq(ppoints(length(x)), df), x,
    pch = 20, col = "darkgreen", main = main,
    xlab = "Theoretical quantiles", ylab = "Empirical quantiles"
  )
  abline(0, 1, col = "red", lwd = 2)
  invisible(NULL)
}

# Plot each of the K node and d = K*(K+1)/2 Lambda components separately.
# Default filtering uses successful replications. Joint squared norms
# are compared with chi-square laws having K and d degrees of freedom.
plot_results <- function(results, config, converged_only = TRUE) {
  rows <- inference_rows(results, converged_only)
  if (!length(rows)) stop("No converged replications available for plotting.")
  x <- results[rows, , drop = FALSE]
  k <- config$k
  d <- k * (k + 1L) / 2L
  old <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), ask = FALSE)
  on.exit(par(old), add = TRUE)

  for (i in seq_len(k)) {
    qqplot_standard_normal(
      x[, paste0("stat_U_", i)],
      paste0(config$model, ": node U coordinate ", i),
      "darkblue"
    )
  }
  qqplot_chisq(x[, "chi_sq_U"], k, paste0("Node U chi-square, df=", k))
  for (i in seq_len(d)) {
    qqplot_standard_normal(
      x[, paste0("raw_lambda_", i)],
```
